newsitem.title: UK: Mediterranean, W.African prompt crude buying thin.
newsitem.headline: Mediterranean, W.African prompt crude buying thin.

text.p: Sour crudes and supplies of some sweet grades in the Mediterranean and West Africa remained ample as poor refining margins kept buying interest thin.
However, while West African prices were talked slightly lower, Mediterranean traders saw little sign of differentials falling from last week's levels despite refiners' expectations of weaker prices.
"It's fair to say that's still the sentiment in the market but it's not been evidenced by much," said a trader.
Traders said a tight fuel oil market was helping to counter the impact of August run cuts forced by stubbornly thin margins.

A couple of 80,000-tonne end-August Urals cargoes continued to weigh on the market. Traders said these were now looking distressed, but the sellers were still holding out for last Fridays dated Brent -90 cent a barrel level.
Some sellers were confident of achieving narrower discounts for later barrels but traders said much would depend on an improvement in refining margins.
Other grades on offer included Syrian Light for mid to late September at around official selling prices and a million barrels of Iranian Heavy loading in the middle of next month.
Most West African crudes were slightly weaker, prompt supplies were seen balanced, but second and third decade September supplies were looking slightly lengthy.
"The big fish have had their fill of the September cargoes it all depends on how the leftovers are mopped up, but most grades are being talked slightly lower," a trader said.

Offers for early September Forcados cargoes were seen steady in balanced trade at values around Dated Brent +35 cents a barrel, but offers later in the month were down to +40 cents compared with +42-44 cents last week.

Bonny Light avails were seen improved after recent loading problems were sorted out and the last few cargoes were loaded on time. Prompt cargoes talked slightly lower at around dated Brent +48/52 cents a barrel.
Avails of two cargoes of third decade Qua Ibo, a prompt Escravos cargo and Cabinda barrels were also seen, but the scant buying interest saw sellers reluctant to make the market.
